review_candidates.description: About MAVI MAVI places experienced finance and accounting professionals into senior, high-ownership roles at high-growth US companies. We maintain a deliberately high bar on both sides of the placement. The companies we partner with are venture-backed and private equity-backed businesses building modern finance organizations, and the professionals we represent are operators with a track record of owning the numbers rather than supporting them from a distance. The roles we place are embedded positions within the finance function itself. Our professionals work alongside founders, CEOs, and senior leadership on the work that determines whether a business can close its books with confidence, satisfy its auditors, raise its next round, and scale. Our team has built and scaled finance functions at companies including Lyft, Ramp, and SoftBank. We remain closely involved throughout the relationship, from role alignment and interview preparation through onboarding, placement, and long-term career development. The Role We are seeking an experienced Head Accountant to own the finance function of a high-growth US company, working remotely from LATAM. This is the senior finance seat in the business, and it remains substantively hands-on. You will be accountable for the accuracy of the financials, the close, the audit, and the controls, and you will carry that ownership through into planning, forecasting, cash management, and the finance infrastructure the company needs in order to keep growing. You will also be the person who builds the close checklist, investigates the variance through to its root cause, and replaces the processes that are no longer serving the business. You will work directly with the founders, CEO, and leadership team. A significant part of the role is translating financial information into clear recommendations that people outside finance can act on. Because you will be the most senior finance person in the company and located outside the United States, the role calls for someone who operates well with autonomy, communicates proactively rather than on request, and can hold both the detail and the strategic picture without a layer above them to catch what falls through. What You'll Own Accounting and Controls The close. Lead the monthly, quarterly, and annual close, with full accountability for the calendar, the quality of the output, and the cycle time. The financial statements. Own the P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement outright, and stand behind the numbers in front of the CEO and the board. The accounting team and partners. Lead the accounting team and manage external accounting, tax, and finance partners, holding each to agreed standards and deadlines. Policies and controls. Establish and maintain accounting policies, internal controls, approval workflows, and reporting standards appropriate to the company's stage. Multi-entity accounting. Own multi-entity accounting and consolidation across the group structure. Audit. Lead the annual audit or review, including auditor management, PBC preparation, and resolution of findings through to close-out. Tax compliance. Coordinate US federal, state, and local tax compliance with external CPA firms. Planning and Strategic Finance Budgeting and forecasting. Lead the annual budget, rolling forecasts, long-range planning, and headcount planning. Financial modelling. Build and maintain the models behind pricing, hiring, compensation, investment, and other strategic decisions. Reporting to leadership. Prepare and present monthly and quarterly reporting to the CEO, leadership team, and board. Business partnership. Work with department leaders on performance, spend, margins, hiring, and the decisions that move the numbers. Fundraising support. Support fundraising and investor diligence, including models, historical financials, data rooms, and investor requests. Cash and Risk Cash and runway. Manage the company's cash position, liquidity, and runway, including a maintained 13-week cash flow forecast. Working capital. Monitor burn, working capital, collections, and significant upcoming payments. Banking. Manage banking relationships and payment approval processes. Risk. Identify financial and operational risks early — runway, customer concentration, collections, covenant exposure — and work with leadership on mitigation. Systems and Scale Finance systems roadmap. Lead ERP selection and implementation, AP and expense automation, and reporting infrastructure. Process design. Build finance processes that improve accuracy, visibility, and efficiency as the company grows, rather than processes that break at the next stage. What We're Looking For 7+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including 3+ years leading and developing a finance or accounting team Genuine depth across both accounting and FP&A, rather than a career specialised exclusively in one Strong command of US GAAP, including revenue recognition (ASC 606), leases (ASC 842), and stock-based compensation (ASC 718) Experience acting as the senior finance partner to founders, CEOs, or boards, including presenting results and defending recommendations Demonstrated ownership of the close and the financial statements on an independent basis, rather than contribution to someone else's Hands-on experience with cash forecasting, liquidity management, and runway planning Substantial ERP experience with NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks Online, or a comparable platform, alongside familiarity with modern finance tooling such as Ramp, Brex, Bill.com, Rippling, Gusto, Carta, or FloQast Experience with multi-entity accounting and consolidation A track record of building finance processes from the ground up, or of taking on underperforming processes and rebuilding them Comfort operating within a lean team, with the seniority to own the function and the willingness to prepare the entry yourself when circumstances require it Experience hiring, managing, and developing accountants or finance analysts Experience working remotely with US-based leadership, auditors, and CPA firms, with the communication discipline that arrangement requires Excellent written and verbal English, with the confidence to hold the room in a board or leadership setting Based in LATAM with the ability to maintain meaningful overlap with US business hours CPA, Contador Público, CA, ACCA, CIMA, or an equivalent professional qualification strongly preferred Experience at a venture-backed or PE-backed US company, particularly from Seed through Series C, preferred Big 4 or comparable public accounting experience followed by industry experience preferred Direct experience carrying a fundraise, a first audit, or an ERP implementation end to end is highly regarded SaaS or recurring-revenue experience, including ARR, NRR, deferred revenue, and unit economics, is a significant advantage Exposure to US multi-state tax, international entities, or transfer pricing is welcome Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field Who This Role Is For This role is well suited to a finance leader who wants to sit close to the business rather than at a distance from it. You move comfortably between accounting detail and financial planning, you build the process the company needs at each stage instead of waiting for one to be handed to you, and you are credible in a room with founders, investors, and auditors alike. Above all, you identify issues early, communicate them clearly to the people who need to know, and arrive with a practical recommendation rather than only a number. Why Join Through MAVI Own an entire finance function, end to end, with direct exposure to founders and senior leadership Take ownership across accounting, FP&A, cash management, and strategic finance in a single seat Build the finance infrastructure of a growing company rather than maintaining someone else's Sit close to the decisions — pricing, hiring, investment, fundraising — with visible impact on the outcome Progress toward Fractional CFO and CFO opportunities through MAVI Work remotely from LATAM with US-based leadership, in near-full overlap with the US business day Receive MAVI's support throughout placement, onboarding, and the engagement that follows Work Arrangement This is a remote role based in LATAM, with meaningful overlap with US business hours. You will work directly with US-based founders, leadership teams, auditors, and external partners.

The position acts as the operational backbone of the HR workstream and contributes to the successful delivery of the HR component of Project Harmony. Coordinate meeting invitations, agendas, supporting documentation, logistics, attendance tracking and follow-up activities, including minutes and action items. Monitor action completion and follow up with action owner on outstanding tasks. Maintain contact lists and stakeholder distribution groups. Documentation and project records management Manage the HR workstream SharePoint site and document repositories. Ensure project documents are correctly named, version controlled, filed and archived. Governance, reporting and tracking support Assist with monitoring progress against HR workstream plans and milestones. Support the preparation of dashboards, status reports and progress updates. Assist in preparing materials for Steering Committee meetings and project reviews. Compile information requested from HR stakeholders, workstream members and project leadership. Stakeholder and regional coordination support Coordinate engagement with HR colleagues across headquarters, regions and country offices. Consolidate feedback received from regional HR teams and project participants. Assist the HR business owner in coordinating communications with HR focal points, core system users, and subject matter experts. HR system selection and procurement support Support administration of Requests for Information (RFI), Requests for Proposal (RFP) and vendor evaluation processes. Compile evaluation documentation and stakeholder feedback. Maintain records of vendor communications and project procurement documents. Support document preparation for procurement reviews and decision-making processes. Data migration and testing coordination support Support and coordinate data validation and data-cleansing activities. Coordinate participation of HR stakeholders in testing activities. Maintain testing schedules, participant lists, testing documentation, and testing feedback. Assist with preparation of testing reports and sign-off documentation. Change management and communication support Assist in preparing HR communications, presentations, FAQs and awareness materials. Support training logistics, participation tracking and follow-up. Assist with coordination of Harmony Ambassadors and regional focal points. Collect and consolidate user feedback and adoption information. Go-live and post-implementation support Support preparation of go-live documentation and checklists. Maintain issue and support logs during implementation and stabilisation periods. Assist in monitoring and reporting post-implementation issues and requests. Support knowledge-transfer and project closure activities. The above job description contains the main duties and responsibilities for this position. However, in an organisation such as IUCN, staff members are expected to show flexibility in their approach to work and be willing to undertake other tasks that are reasonably allocated to them, but which are not part of their regular job description. Where any task becomes a regular part of an employee's responsibilities, the job description will be changed in consultation with the employee and the Human Resources Management Group. Requirements Education: Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in Business Administration, Human Resources, Information Systems, Project Management or related field. Relevant certifications in HRIS, project management, change management, or data analysis would be an asset. Experience & technical skills: Minimum 3 years’ experience in providing project, programme, HR or administrative support. Experience working with HR information systems and employee data management. Experience in an international and multicultural environment. Exposure to HRIS, ERP or digital transformation projects. Knowledge of data cleansing, data migration, and data validation methodologies. Other Skills: Outstanding attention to details and data accuracy. Strong sense of discretion in handling information that is private or confidential in nature. Ability to work under tight deadlines and with multiple priorities. Excellent organization and coordination skills. Ability to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders. Languages: Excellent written and spoken English is required. Basic to intermediate knowledge of Spanish would be an asset. SALARY The minimum gross annual salary for this position is EUR 34'200. While this is an indicative amount effective as of the current date, changes may occur as per IUCN's compensation practices without prior notice. The same applies to other organisations hosted by IUCN. APPLICATIONS Applicants are requested to apply online through the HR Management System, by opening the vacancy announcement and pressing the "Apply" button. Applicants will be asked to create an account and submit their profile information. Applications will not be accepted after the closing date. The vacancy closes at midnight, Swiss time (GMT+1 / GMT+2 during Daylight Saving Time, DST). Please note that only selected applicants will be personally contacted for interviews. Other job opportunities are published in the IUCN website: https://www.iucn.org/involved/jobs/ About IUCN IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together. Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 16,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards. IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development. Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being. www.iucn.org https://twitter.com/IUCN

review_candidates.description: About Us QISG leverages Quanta’s comprehensive resources to deliver collaborative solutions for our partners' energy infrastructure needs. We use in-house talent, expertise and resources to plan, design, engineer, manage, conduct maintenance on and construct projects. Our turnkey service capabilities provide our customers with efficiency, consistency, attention to detail and safe execution. The QISG team brings together Engineering, Safety, Quality, Material Procurement, QA/QC, Right-of-Way Acquisition, Scheduling, Environmental Planning, Permitting, Title and Land Management expertise that ensure outstanding results for our clients. About This Role Job Title: Director, Engineering PMO - Transmission Line At QISG, our Transmission Line organization is central to the safe, reliable, and efficient delivery of power across communities and regions. We design, build, maintain, and upgrade high-voltage transmission infrastructure that forms the backbone of the electric grid. The Engineering Director – PMO provides enterprise-level leadership for transmission line engineering delivery, ensuring technical excellence, consistency, scalability, and alignment with QISG’s strategic objectives. This role leads the Engineering Project Management Office (PMO) for Transmission Lines across the QISG platform and is accountable for engineering governance, portfolio performance, resource strategy, and continuous improvement. The Director partners closely with executive leadership, operations, customers, and Quanta Operating Units to ensure engineering capabilities effectively support growth, execution certainty, and long-term value creation. What You'll Do Provide enterprise leadership for the Transmission Line Engineering PMO, setting vision, strategy, and priorities aligned with QISG business objectives. Establish and maintain engineering governance frameworks, standards, and controls across the full project lifecycle (concept through closeout). Ensure consistent application of engineering policies, procedures, risk management, and quality systems across all transmission projects. Serve as a senior advisor to executive leadership on engineering strategy, capacity, risk, and performance. Oversee a portfolio of transmission line programs and projects, ensuring alignment with schedule, budget, quality, and safety objectives. Implement portfolio-level performance management, including dashboards, KPIs, and executive reporting. Drive early identification and mitigation of technical, resourcing, and execution risks across the portfolio. Ensure effective integration between engineering, construction, procurement, and operations at a programmatic level. Lead, develop, and mentor Engineering Project Managers and senior engineering leaders across the platform. Define and execute engineering workforce strategy, including staffing models, succession planning, and capability development. Establish training, competency, and professional development frameworks to support current needs and future growth. Foster a high-performance culture emphasizing accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Set strategy and oversight for engineering service providers, consultants, and design partners. Define, monitor, and enforce service provider KPIs, performance standards, and contractual compliance. Partner with senior leadership of engineering firms to drive quality, innovation, and capacity alignment with QISG needs. Support and influence business development strategy by providing executive-level engineering input into pursuits, proposals, and risk reviews. Participate in key client engagements as an engineering authority and trusted advisor. Ensure engineering approaches are scalable, competitive, and aligned with customer expectations and regulatory requirements. Drive innovation and efficiency in engineering delivery through standardized processes, digital tools, and emerging technologies. Partner with Quanta Engineering and Construction OpUs to harmonize best practices and eliminate inefficiencies. Set the tone and expectations for a culture of safety, quality, and integrity across the engineering organization. Ensure engineering decisions and practices align with QISG’s core values and safety commitments. Perform other duties as assigned in support of QISG’s strategic and operational objectives. What You'll Bring Minimum of 15 years of progressive experience in the electric utility industry, with demonstrated leadership in engineering, program management, and/or management of high-voltage transmission projects across multiple phases and regions. Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree in Engineering from an ABET-accredited university required; Master’s degree or equivalent graduate education in Engineering, Business, or Project Management strongly preferred. Professional Engineer (P.E.) license preferred, with the ability to serve as a recognized technical authority and executive engineering leader. Proven track record of leading large, multidisciplinary engineering organizations and portfolios, delivering complex, high-risk transmission programs safely, on schedule, and within budget. Deep technical expertise in structural, civil, or electrical engineering, with the ability to provide executive-level technical oversight, governance, and risk-based decision-making. Expert-level knowledge of electric utility engineering and construction standards, with experience establishing and enforcing enterprise engineering policies, procedures, and controls. Strong understanding of utility industry business processes, including program scheduling, contracting strategies, procurement, project controls, estimating, and coordination across engineering, construction, and operations. Demonstrated financial and business acumen, including experience managing departmental and portfolio-level budgets, forecasting resource needs, and aligning engineering strategy with business objectives. Extensive experience with project controls, cost estimating, risk management, and performance reporting at a program or portfolio level. Proven ability to interpret complex internal and external business issues, set strategic direction, implement best practices, mitigate enterprise risk, and resolve highly complex technical and organizational challenges. Demonstrated success in executive-level customer engagement, supporting key clients, participating in pursuits, and serving as a trusted engineering and delivery advisor. Exceptional leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence at all organizational levels and collaborate effectively with executives, clients, regulators, and external partners. Demonstrated ability to develop and execute long-term strategic plans, drive innovation, standardization, and continuous improvement across engineering organizations. Comprehensive knowledge of applicable industry codes, standards, and regulations, including but not limited to ANSI, ASTM, ACI, AISC, IEEE, NEC, NESC, and relevant federal, state, and utility-specific requirements. Proven ability to lead in ambiguous, fast-paced, and complex environments, balancing competing priorities while maintaining strategic focus and execution discipline.
